html:
World War II was the global war of 1939 to 1945 between the Allies, led by Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States and China, and the Axis powers of Germany, Japan and Italy. It was the deadliest war in history: some 70 to 85 million people died, most of them civilians. It is the second half of what the chart shows as the world wars.

  • Japan had been at war in China since 1937.
  • Hitler's Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France declared war. Germany overran France in 1940, but Britain under Churchill held out.
  • In June 1941 Germany invaded the Soviet Union of Stalin, where most of the fighting and dying in Europe took place.
  • Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941 brought the United States into the war.
  • Behind the front lines Germany carried out the Holocaust, murdering about six million Jews.
  • Germany surrendered in May 1945. After the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Japan surrendered on 2 September 1945.

The war reached far beyond the battlefields. In Africa, British and Ethiopian forces drove Italy out of Ethiopia in 1941. In America, labour shortages brought Mexican workers north under the Bracero Program and sped the Great Migration of Black Americans to factory cities. Afterwards the United Nations was founded, the United States and the Soviet Union faced off in the Cold War, and Europe's empires in Asia and Africa began to fall apart.
